slides.0.title: GI Classification: Zone / Region / Sub-Region
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 1 · Lesson 4
slides.1.title: The Three-Tier GI System
slides.1.points.0: GI = Geographical Indication — Australia's appellation system regulated by AGWA
slides.1.points.1: Tier 1 Zone: the broadest level (e.g. South Australia, South Eastern Australia)
slides.1.points.2: Tier 2 Region: the most commonly seen on labels (e.g. Barossa Valley, Clare Valley)
slides.1.points.3: Tier 3 Sub-Region: the most precise level (e.g. Eden Valley within Barossa Zone)
slides.1.note: To label a wine with a Region name, at least 85% of grapes must come from that Region
slides.2.title: South Australia GI Zones
slides.2.points.0: Barossa Zone: Barossa Valley + Eden Valley — SA's most famous wine zone
slides.2.points.1: Mount Lofty Ranges Zone: Clare Valley, Adelaide Hills, Adelaide Plains
slides.2.points.2: Fleurieu Zone: McLaren Vale, Langhorne Creek, Currency Creek
slides.2.points.3: Limestone Coast Zone: Coonawarra, Wrattonbully, Padthaway, Winemakers from Coonawarra
slides.3.title: 'South Eastern Australia' GI — The Super Zone
slides.3.points.0: The 'South Eastern Australia' GI covers SA, VIC and NSW simultaneously
slides.3.points.1: Used for large-volume commercial wines sourced from multiple states
slides.3.points.2: Common on supermarket labels — Yellow Tail, Hardys, Wolf Blass entry-range
slides.3.points.3: Not a quality indicator — blending across a huge area allows consistent pricing
slides.3.points.4: Key distinction: a wine labelled 'Barossa Valley' must come 85% from Barossa Valley
slides.4.question: A wine bottle labelled 'Barossa Valley' must have what minimum percentage of grapes from that region?
slides.4.explanation: Australian GI regulations require at least 85% of grapes to originate from the named region. This ensures the label accurately reflects the wine's geographic origin — though blending up to 15% from elsewhere is permitted.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: Three GI tiers: Zone (broadest) → Region (most common on labels) → Sub-Region (most precise)
slides.5.points.1: SA GI zones include Barossa, Mount Lofty Ranges, Fleurieu, Limestone Coast
slides.5.points.2: 'South Eastern Australia' is a super zone covering SA, VIC and NSW — used for large commercial blends
